G1.question: Google outputs (Gemini Omni, Veo, Lyria, Gemini image and TTS on the paid Gemini API): may PG1 resell them to clients?
G1.detail: The Gemini API Additional Terms say Google does not claim ownership of generated content and that paid-tier data is not used to improve products, but they grant no express commercial licence. The Google APIs Terms (Section 5, prohibitions on content) bar selling or distributing content returned by an API unless its owner or the law allows it; whether that clause reaches generated output is not answered on Google's pages.
G1.answered: Answered 2026-10-14 by the operator: the Gemini API Additional Terms (effective 25 Sep 2025) say "Google won't claim ownership over that content", make the user responsible for its use and do not ban selling generated output. Gemini, Veo, Imagen and Gemini TTS output through the Gemini API is commercial_ok: operator accepted Google's generated-content terms; operator responsible for use.

G2.question: Lyria music on the paid Gemini API: may it be published and sold, including on streaming platforms and YouTube?
G2.detail: Same terms as G1. Lyria output carries a SynthID watermark. Google's pages give no music-specific rights table, unlike ElevenLabs'.
G2.answered: Answered 2026-10-14 by the operator: the same as G1, so Lyria through the Gemini API is commercial_ok (operator accepted Google's generated-content terms; operator responsible for use) and film music on it may be offered. Lyria 2 through Replicate stays unclear under R1.

R1.question: Replicate-hosted models (Kling, FLUX Kontext Pro, FLUX schnell, Topaz, FILM): what does each model's own licence allow?
R1.detail: Replicate grants its rights in outputs, including commercial use, "subject to any third-party terms" of the model used. The model pages' licence tabs could not be loaded, so each model's terms are unconfirmed.

E1.question: Which ElevenLabs plan is ELEVENLABS_API_KEY on?
E1.detail: Paid plans include a commercial licence; the free plan does not and requires attribution. Eleven Music on self-serve plans excludes film, TV, radio and large studio games (Enterprise only). Streaming distribution needs Creator or above.
E1.answered: Answered 2026-10-14 by the operator: the Creator plan (paid self-serve), with ELEVENLABS_API_KEY set in Vercel (the key is named PG1-Studi0 in ElevenLabs). Creator includes Professional Voice Cloning of the account holder's own voice. ElevenLabs TTS, dialogue, sound effects and voice output are commercial_ok on it. The plan's Eleven Music licence excludes film, TV, radio and large studio games, so film beds stay on Lyria through the Gemini API (lib/film/providers.mjs filmMusicExclude) unless PG1_ELEVENLABS_FILM_RIGHTS=1 records that the plan covers film.

E2.question: Is Eleven v3 Text to Dialogue still a Beta Service?
E2.detail: Content made with ElevenLabs Beta Services cannot be used commercially or in production.
E2.answered: Answered 2026-10-14 by the operator: ElevenLabs' own Eleven v3 page says v3 is no longer in alpha and is generally available, including the Text to Dialogue API endpoint. No beta restriction applies.

T1.question: OpenRouter, the AI gateway and OpenAI: may their output go into a client deliverable?
T1.detail: Google (G1, G2), ElevenLabs (E1) and Claude (cleared by the operator on 2026-10-16) have an answer for client work. Until this one is answered, a client job's text (storyboards, scripts, checks) runs on Claude, then the paid Gemini key; the operator's own films keep the whole text chain.

C1.question: Cartesia (the voice PG1 Studio uses now for voice-over): do its terms allow resale of output?
C1.detail: Cartesia was outside this phase's providers (Replicate, Google, ElevenLabs), so its terms were not reviewed.
